Three lines tell you everything about where Web3 is headed.

DeFi TVL dominates. It dipped in 2023, recovered, and is now higher than ever. The protocols that survived the bear market are the ones actually generating revenue.

NFT volume peaked in 2022 and has not recovered. The speculative phase is over. What remains is infrastructure. Digital identity, on-chain credentials, tokenized assets.

DAO treasuries are the quiet story. Slow, steady growth. Organizations are accumulating capital and governance is maturing.

The capital flows tell you where the jobs will be. DeFi and infrastructure roles are growing. Pure NFT roles are shrinking. DAO operations is emerging as a real career path.

Follow the capital. Find the careers.

linkedin.text:
Ethereum Layer 2s now process more daily transactions than Ethereum itself.

Base leads with 5.2 million transactions per day. Arbitrum follows at 2.8 million. Optimism sits at 1.1 million. Ethereum L1 also sits at 1.1 million.

Read that again. Coinbase's Base alone processes nearly 5x the volume of Ethereum mainnet.

This is the infrastructure shift happening in plain sight. Developers are building on L2s because the economics make sense. Users are transacting on L2s because the fees make sense.

The teams building on these chains need engineers, product managers, and researchers. That is where the roles are opening up fastest.

linkedin.text:
In 2021, you paid $300 in gas to mint a JPEG.

In 2026, you pay $0.001 on Base to deploy a smart contract.

Five years of infrastructure work made that possible. Rollups, data availability layers, EIP-4844, proto-danksharding. The engineers who built this rarely get credit for it.

The gas fee chart going to near zero is not an accident. It is the result of thousands of engineers solving one of the hardest problems in distributed systems.

Those same teams are still hiring. And the next wave of problems is just as hard.

linkedin.text:
Bitcoin ETFs crossed $100 billion in assets under management.

BlackRock iShares holds 48% of that. Fidelity holds 22%. ARK and 21Shares at 8%. Bitwise at 7%. The rest is spread across a dozen smaller issuers.

Two years ago, the idea of BlackRock managing a Bitcoin fund would have sounded absurd. Now they manage nearly half of all spot Bitcoin ETF assets.

This is not just a capital story. It is a talent story. Every one of these firms is hiring compliance teams, blockchain analysts, custody engineers, and fund operations specialists who understand both TradFi and crypto.

The bridge between Wall Street and Web3 is being built right now. And there are roles on both sides.

linkedin.text:
The stablecoin market went from $20 billion in 2020 to over $210 billion in 2026.

Six years. 10x growth. And most people outside of crypto have no idea this happened.

Stablecoins are now the most used product in all of crypto. More than DeFi. More than NFTs. More than any L1 or L2 token. They are the payment rails, the settlement layer, and the unit of account for an entire parallel financial system.

Tether and Circle alone process more daily volume than most traditional payment networks.

The teams building stablecoin infrastructure, compliance frameworks, and cross-border payment products need people who understand both financial regulation and blockchain architecture.

Those roles exist today.
